findings.where: "Where we're starting" destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok), with their "Best hostels >" lines, on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The cards look like links. Each one has its own box, a hover rule, a line in the link colour and a chevron. But none of them goes anywhere: the parts map lists all three as static. The page is meant to send visitors to the destination guides, and right now nothing on it reaches a guide. "Explore destinations" and the nav's "Destinations" both lead only to this dead end.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who taps Canggu to see its hostels gets no response. They decide the site is broken or empty and leave. The page's third job, routing people to the guides, fails completely.

findings.where: Nav "How we rank", and the footer's "How we rank", "Privacy", "Terms" and "Report content"
findings.fault: Every one of these links points back to this same page. They look real (the footer ones are underlined, and the nav one is styled like a link) but they lead nowhere.
findings.who_objects: The whole pitch is merit-only ranking. A visitor who clicks "How we rank" to check that claim, or "Privacy" before sending an email, lands back where they started. That undercuts the trust the page is asking for.

findings.where: Destination cards: the eyebrows (BALI, LOMBOK) and the place names
findings.fault: The cards are set in a monospace typewriter face, not the brand's Quicksand headings and Nunito Sans labels. It looks like unstyled code or a broken font, and nothing else on the page uses it.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because it breaks the brand's set type pairing in its most visible content block. Visitors would also object: a typewriter face on travel cards looks unfinished, and the brand names sterile or broken as its enemy.

findings.where: Destination cards: the border and the shadow
findings.fault: The cards have a thick purple border, a colour that isn't in the palette and does no job there. They also sit under a heavy, wide shadow while at rest. The rules call for a 1–1.5 px sand-border edge and no heavy shadow at rest.
findings.who_objects: The founder: the brand gives every colour exactly one job and keeps the field to turquoise and sand. A stray purple and drop-shadow boxes make this section look like it came from a different site.

findings.where: Whole page, squinting: the hero's headline against the "Where we're starting" heading (desktop especially)
findings.fault: The section heading "Where we're starting" is set far larger than anything in the hero. On desktop it takes up most of the bottom of the first screen and is the loudest thing on the page. In the hero, the biggest text is the brand name, which the nav already shows. The actual promise ("ranks on merit alone, then sends you to book with the hostel") is in small body text, and the eyebrow line is a vague "The better way".
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning for a few seconds sees the brand name and a section heading, not what the site does for them. The founder positions on findability through merit ranking, and that claim loses to a section label.

findings.where: Hero buttons: the coral "Email … for launch news" and the outlined "Explore destinations"
findings.fault: The two buttons have different shapes. The coral one is a full pill and the outline one has square corners, while the rules give both buttons the 8 px control radius. The coral label is also a whole sentence with the full address in it, so on phone it wraps to two lines.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because a controls system meant to be consistent here uses two shapes for one kind of thing. Phone visitors get a two-line slab where a short verb would read at a glance.

findings.where: Hero primary action, the launch-news email link
findings.fault: Signing up means writing an email from scratch to a personal address. The page doesn't say what to write, or whether replying will sign you up. Phones without a mail app set up do nothing when it's tapped.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone mid-trip who would gladly leave an address for launch news, but won't compose an email to a stranger. The page's main contact-collection job loses most of its sign-ups.

findings.where: Footer status line, "Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali", against the destination cards
findings.fault: The footer says the pilot is in Bali only, but the "Where we're starting" section lists Kuta Lombok as a starting place.
findings.who_objects: A visitor planning Lombok can't tell whether it's covered. Mismatched facts make a pre-launch site look careless.

findings.where: Desktop: left edges of the nav, the hero text column and the destinations section
findings.fault: The hero copy starts in an indented column, about 230 px further in than the nav wordmark and the section below it. Those two share one left edge, so the hero sits off the page's grid.
findings.who_objects: A designer or founder reviewing the launch page will see it as misaligned. The eye has to find a new start line between the nav, the hero and the cards.

findings.where: Nav links on desktop: "Destinations" against "How we rank"
findings.fault: "How we rank" is underlined and "Destinations" is not. Two links of the same kind get different treatments, and the underline looks like it marks the current page, even though this page is neither one.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reads the underlined item as "you are here" or as more important. The founder's rule gives nav links one treatment and marks the current page with semibold.
